# dsh-plugin-session-spend

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that shows what the current
session has cost so far, split by DeepSeek's p
eak and off-peak rate windows.
**English** | 中文
## What it shows
A pill in the composer dock, beside the shipped token-usage pill:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Click it for the breakdown. A session that stayed inside one window shows a single block:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A session spanning both windows splits into two blocks, each with its own subtotal:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The figure is the **whole session**, not the loaded window: paging, compaction, and
resuming a sessi
on do not change it, and a retried model request is not billed twice.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The script does two things: copies the package to `<profile>\plugins\session-cost\`, and
appends the

mount entry to `<profile>\cordis.patch.yml` (skipped when it is already there).
Then **refresh the
DSH page (Ctrl+R)**.

The profile directory is resolved in this order: the `-ProfileDir` argument, then
`$env:DSH_PROFILE_
DIR`, then `~\.dsh\profiles\desktop`.

`-ExecutionPolicy Bypass` is needed because Windows blocks unsigned `.ps1` files by
default. On a ma

chine whose execution policy already allows local scripts, `.\install.ps1`
works as-is. On macOS or
Linux, do the same two steps by hand under PowerShell 7.
### Upgrading an existing install

Re-running `install.ps1` overwrites the files in place, which is enough for a normal version
bump. *

*A release that renames the package is the exception**: DSH caches a plugin's resolved
package name

at load time, while the client bundle registers under the new one, so the browser
half fails to load

even though every file on disk is correct. The script detects that case and
warns — restart DSH, th

en run it again. Reloading the page is not enough, because the stale
name lives in the host process.
## Configure

Edit the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` and save — the patch layer is watched, so no restart
is needed
. Refresh the page afterwards so the browser picks up the new rates.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The built-in defaults are **DeepSeek `deepseek-flash` off-peak list prices** in CNY per
million toke
ns, taken from the official pricing page on 2026-10-15:
| | Off-peak | Peak |

| Input (cache hit) | ¥0.02 | ¥0.04 |
| Input (cache miss) | ¥1 | ¥2 |
| Output | ¥4 | ¥8 |

**Check them against your own bill.** A third-party gateway does not bill these numbers,
and this ta
ble covers only `deepseek-flash`.
## Limitations

- **Holidays are yours to fill in.** `holidays` defaults to empty. China's public holidays
are annou

nced yearly and cannot be derived, so top the list up each year. Weekends that
are worked as make-up

days stay off-peak: the published rule only looks at Monday-Friday
plus the holiday list.
- **One r

ate table, not one per model.** Switching models mid-session is not detected; every
token is priced

with the same rates.
- **Reasoning tokens are not added on top.** `reasoningTokens` is a subset of w

hat output is
billed for, so adding it would double-count.
- **An estimate, not an invoice.** Token

cost only — no minimum spend, tiered pricing,
currency conversion, or granted credit.
- **The peak w
indow is fixed** at Beijing time Monday-Friday 09:00-12:00 and 14:00-18:00.

The design behind the numbers, and the DSH internals this plugin had to work around, are in
docs/IMP

nd the numbers, and the DSH internals this plugin had to work around, are in
docs/IMPLEMENTATION.md.
## Development
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`check.mjs` needs nothing but Node: it renders the client half through a small React
stand-in that c
overs exactly the API surface the component uses.

`check-host.mjs` imports the host half, which resolves `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` and `zod`
from its

own location — both are supplied by DeepSeek Harness. Point it at an installed copy
(the normal cas

e), or install those two packages first. Run it with no argument and it says
so instead of failing s

nstall those two packages first. Run it with no argument and it says
so instead of failing silently.
## Releasing

Publishing happens in CI, never from a laptop: `.github/workflows/publish.yml`
publishes on a `v*` t

ag through npm **Trusted Publishing** (OIDC), so this repository holds no
`NPM_TOKEN` and no long-li

ved write credential — nothing to leak and nothing to rotate.
Provenance attestations are attached a
utomatically for a public package in a public repository.

1. Bump `version` in `package.json` and commit.
2. `git tag v0.1.0 && git push origin v0.1.0`.

The tag-driven run needs a Trusted Publisher configured once on npmjs.com: the package's
Settings →

Trusted Publisher → GitHub Actions, with user `dtxovo`, repository
`dsh-plugin-session-spend`, and w
orkflow `publish.yml`.
